# ♻️ ReCircle — Waste Exchange Platform

> One person's waste is another's raw material.

**ReCircle** is a circular-economy marketplace where waste generated by one person becomes a resource for someone else nearby. A restaurant lists its leftover cardboard boxes, a student finds them for a college project; someone lists unused electronics, a recycler picks them up. Every completed hand-off is recorded, and the community can see how much material has been kept out of landfill.

Submitted to **TERRACODE 2026**, the online website development competition by **FOSS Club, MEA Engineering College**.

Theme: ***Green Tomorrow — Building a Sustainable Future***

## The problem

Usable materials such as cardboard, glass jars, fabric offcuts, old electronics and scrap metal are thrown away every day, while students, small businesses and recyclers nearby are looking for exactly those things. There is no simple local place where the two sides can find each other.

## Our solution

ReCircle connects **waste generators** (households, shops, restaurants) with **people who can reuse materials** (students, makers, recyclers). Users list what they have or post what they need, find matches on a map, chat to arrange pickup, and confirm the exchange together. Confirmed exchanges feed a public impact dashboard.

## ✨ Features

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Waste listing & categories** | Post an *Available* offer or a *Wanted* request in 10 material categories with quantity, weight, condition, price (or free) and a photo. |
| **Location-based discovery** | Map of listings (OpenStreetMap), distance filter, nearest-first sorting and "Use my location". The pickup area name is filled in automatically from the map pin. |
| **Buyer–seller messaging** | Real-time chat between the two people, suggested quick replies and unread badges. |
| **Two-way exchange confirmation** | Both people confirm the hand-off. A confirmation can be undone until the other person confirms, and an exchanged item can't be reopened. |
| **Exchange history** | Community and personal timelines with category filter and CSV export. |
| **Recycling impact dashboard** | Kilograms diverted, estimated CO₂e avoided, monthly and per-material charts, everyday equivalents and a contributor leaderboard. |
| **⭐ Circular matches** | Every listing shows nearby people on the other side of the loop: offers for a wanted item and requests for an offered item. This is what makes ReCircle a circular-economy marketplace rather than a classifieds page. |
| **Accounts** | Sign-up with email confirmation, password reset, editable profile (individual, student, business or recycler) and account deletion. |
| **Safety & privacy** | Report listings, approximate pickup locations only (about 100 m), rate limits, and row-level security on every table. |
| **Usability** | Responsive layout for phones, dark mode and keyboard-accessible dialogs. |

## 🛠️ Built with free & open-source tools

| Tool | License | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| HTML, CSS, JavaScript | — | The whole website, no build step |
| [Supabase](https://supabase.com) (PostgreSQL, Auth, Storage, Realtime) | Apache-2.0 | Accounts, database, photo storage, live chat |
| [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com) 1.9.4 | BSD-2-Clause | Maps |
| [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) & Nominatim | ODbL | Map tiles and area names |
| [Chart.js](https://www.chartjs.org) 4 | MIT | Impact charts |
| Fraunces & DM Sans fonts | SIL OFL | Typography |
| GitHub Pages | — | Free hosting |

Leaflet, Chart.js, the Supabase client library and the fonts are bundled in `vendor/` and `assets/fonts/`, so the site doesn't depend on third-party CDNs.

## 🧭 How it works

```
List waste ──► Discover nearby ──► Chat & agree ──► Both confirm ──► History & impact
 (post.html)    (marketplace.html)  (messages.html)   (messages.html)   (history / impact)
```

- **Frontend:** static pages served by GitHub Pages.
- **Backend:** Supabase. Data is protected with PostgreSQL Row Level Security. Sensitive actions such as completing an exchange, undoing a confirmation and deleting an account run as database functions, so they can't be faked from the browser.
- **Photos:** resized in the browser to a full image and a thumbnail, then stored in Supabase Storage (300 KB limit, JPEG only).

## 🚀 Run it locally

1. Clone the repository and open the folder in VS Code.
2. Install the **Live Server** extension.
3. Right-click `index.html` → **Open with Live Server**.

The site connects to our Supabase project out of the box. Only the public *publishable* key is in the code; access is controlled by Row Level Security.

## 🗄️ Set up your own Supabase backend (optional)

1. Create a free project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2. In **SQL Editor**, run these in order:
   1. `supabase/schema.sql`
   2. `supabase/migration-v2.sql`
   3. `supabase/migration-v3.sql`
3. **Authentication → URL Configuration:** set the Site URL to your site address and add it under Redirect URLs (including `reset.html`).
4. **Authentication → Emails:** set up a custom SMTP sender, and paste `supabase/confirm-signup-email.html` into the *Confirm signup* template.
5. Put your project URL and publishable key in `js/supabase.js`.

## 🌍 Impact calculation

CO₂e avoided = material weight × a per-material factor (see `CATEGORIES` in `js/data.js`). These are indicative estimates for awareness, not certified figures. The dashboard's equivalents use common reference values: about 21 kg CO₂ absorbed per tree per year, 0.17 kg CO₂ per km in a petrol car, and 0.008 kg CO₂ per smartphone charge.

## 🔒 Privacy

- Only an approximate pickup point is stored; exact addresses are shared privately in chat.
- Chats are visible only to the two people in them.
- Users can delete their account at any time. See [`privacy.html`](privacy.html).
